brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: 7 bin parts placed on 7 hexagonal bases: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 comps), bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2), bin:-1,1,0~hex-bin-full (1), bin:0,-1,0~hex-bin-half-div3 (3), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-half-div2 (2), bin:1,-1,0~hex-bin-full (1), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2). Each bin is a separate container, totaling 14 compartments, exceeding the minimum of six.

Compact 7-cell honeycomb (center + 6 around) with mixed full/half depth and divided bins for sorting screws/nuts/standoffs. Dressed with 14 small hardware props (heap-screws/nuts/standoffs in div2/div3 variants) seated in compartments; top-down view (polar 10°) shows all compartments and hardware.

finish.summary: Built a 7-bin (14-compartment) small-parts organizer on a 7-cell honeycomb base (center 0,0 plus six neighbours). Used varied bins: two full plain, two full-div2, one full-div3, one half-div3, one half-div2 to provide shallow and deep sorting. All open faces capped and joints locked, verified with check_build mesh clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
